title: Permutations
statement: Return every permutation of a list of distinct integers, in any order. The list has at least one element.
reference_solution:
def permute(nums):
    res, cur = [], []
    used = [False] * len(nums)
    def bt():
        if len(cur) == len(nums):
            res.append(cur[:])
            return
        for i in range(len(nums)):
            if used[i]:
                continue
            used[i] = True
            cur.append(nums[i])
            bt()
            cur.pop()
            used[i] = False
    bt()
    return res

hints.1_question: Build a permutation one position at a time. What choices are available at each position?
hints.2_nudge: At each step try every element not yet used, recurse, then undo the choice (backtrack).
hints.3_big_hint: If len(cur) == n: record a COPY. Else for each unused i: mark used, append, recurse, pop, unmark.
